newsitem.title: EGYPT: Get serious about peace, PLO spokesman tells U.S..
newsitem.headline: Get serious about peace, PLO spokesman tells U.S..

text.p: A Palestinian spokesman said on Friday the Middle East peace process was "clinically dead" and called on the United States to resurrect it .
Marwan Kanafani, spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said Arafat sent a letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton saying Clinton must act quickly to save the peace process.
He was speaking at a news conference in Cairo after U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross' efforts in Israel failed to breathe life into deadlocked Israeli-Palestinian peace moves.
Kanafani said Ross's trip was a "complete failure".

"The peace process is clinically dead. We need a last effort to save it," Kanafani said. "It's about time the international community and especially the government of the United States take a serious step, a last attempt to save the peace process."

Ross was due to leave Israel on Friday after he failed to budge the two sides from positions hardened during a two-month peace freeze since Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem on March 18.
The PLO demands Israel halt the settlement, which it sees as an attempt to pre-empt final talks on Jerusalem's status.
Kanafani was due to meet Egyptian officials and European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos on Saturday. He said Palestinians were also seeking help from Russia, Japan, and other countries.

"The American mediation is built on the fact that they cannot do anything about the settlements and let's talk about something else. This is not the mediation that in fact could save the peace process," he said. "We have something against the seriousness of the American government."

He referred to appointments of former U.S. secretaries of state James Baker and Cyrus Vance as mediators in southern Sahara and Bosnia-Herzegovina. "Why such an effort and such personality was not chosen to deal with the Middle East. Some Palestinians take this as an indicator of the seriousness of the American government.
"Why are their (American) efforts always to justify or be apologetic for the Israeli actions and persuading the Palestinians to give more concessions?" Kanafani said.
Kanafani said he hoped a meeting between Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Washington on Friday with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would help put the process on track.
Kanafani said the Palestinians wanted Israel to stop building settlements and "be serious" about redeployments and "that might open the door to going back to negotiations."
Kanafani said scheduling problems prevented Arafat from meeting Ross on the eve of the U.S. envoy's departure.
